I read "In the Matter of J. R. Oppenheimer" a play by the German author Heinar Kipphardt, who was important for documentary theatre amazon link to the book. German title "In der Sache J Robert Oppenheimer, ein szenischer Bericht".

The play is about the proceeding of the Atomic Energy commission regarding Oppenheimer's top secret security clearance regarding his political views and loyalty. The main theme is the relation of science, ethics and freedom. I highly recommend reading the piece, though it is not for everyone, and is a bit controversial (e.g. Oppenheimer objected to the play).

The questions that arise throughout the play are fascinating. Some physicists from the Manhattan project are in the stand as witnesses. Edward Teller (father of the hydrogen bomb) as ideological counter part to Oppenheimer, Enrico Fermi and Hans Bethe.

I was really impressed by the whole piece. The quote you mentioned instantly stuck in my head, as it is simultaneously beautiful in its wording and destructive in its meaning.

Kipphardt translated the verse in his piece like this:

Ich bin der Tod

der alles raubt

Erschütterer der Welten

Rough English translation:

I am death

Who robs everything

Shatterer of worlds

About Kipphardt's play from the description at Amazon:

Kipphardt uses the facts taken from the published transcript to present some fundamental issues which face the world today--the conflict between the responsibility of the individual to his country and to humanity as a whole, the right of the patriot to express views at odds with those of his government without his loyalty being called into question.

I recently nuked the Windows partition from the laptop I bought, so now I only have Debian, but the Microsoft bootloader is still in /boot/efi/EFI/Microsoft and it seems the default to boot is set to Windows, which it can't find now.

I was wondering whether I could completely get rid of the EFI partition and install legacy grub, or if that's a bad idea and we should all migrate to UEFI sooner or later anyhow? If the latter, I guess that efibootmgr would let me kick out the Windows default and make it boot Debian always?
Going from UEFI to legacy boot, a good idea?

I know this is old, but for posterity:

Rename the Microsoft .efi files and use efibootmgr to set grub EFI as the priority. Nothing to worry about. I successfully set up an EFI Windows/Debian dual-boot that way and it works like a dream.

It did not work for me, apparently because the Acer laptop I have has a buggy BIOS. The solution was to switch Secure Boot on, "bless" the Grub .xfi file in the BIOS, then set it to be the first in the boot list and switch Secure Boot off again. I was only able to change the boot order in the BIOS (any setting from efibootmgr would be ignored). I don't know what the hell this BIOS does, but it's surprisingly buggy.

Renaming the EFI files would just lead to various different errors from whatever remnants of the Microsoft loader were still there. Oh well! I think on a system that actually implements UEFI more or less properly, things would work easily with efibootmgr.
